title: Apostle to the apostles (John 20:11–18)
hook: Mary Magdalene is sent to tell the others; Pope Francis raised her day to a feast in 2016

segments.voice: Yesterday, blood and water from the opened side. Your line was they shall look on him.

Early Sunday morning, still dark. Mary Magdalene has come to the tomb and found the stone rolled away. She ran for Peter and the beloved disciple. They came running, saw the linen cloths lying there, and went home. She didn't. She's standing outside the tomb, crying. It's the kind of crying where you can't leave, because leaving would make it real. Everyone else has gone. And she's the one who stays.
screen: `THE STONE ROLLED AWAY.` → `THE MEN GO HOME.` → `SHE STAYS, CRYING.`

segments.voice: She stoops to look into the tomb and sees two angels where the body had been. Woman, why weepest thou? Because they have taken away my Lord, she says, and I know not where they have laid him. She turns and sees a man she takes for the gardener. Sir, if you've carried him off, tell me where, and I'll take him away. Then he says one word. In the Douay-Rheims: "Jesus saith to her: Mary. She turning, saith to him: Rabboni (which is to say, Master)." Not a speech. Her name. The good shepherd said his sheep know his voice when he calls them by name, and here it happens. Then Jesus says, do not touch me, for I am not yet ascended. The Latin, noli me tangere, gave its name to many paintings. The Greek may mean something closer to, don't hold on to me, don't cling. Because she has a job. Go to my brethren, he says, and tell them. And she does. The text says: Mary Magdalen cometh and telleth the disciples, "I have seen the Lord," and what he said to her. In John's telling, she's the one sent with the news, sent to the apostles themselves. Christian writers came to give her a title for it: apostle to the apostles. Apostle means one who is sent. In 2016 Pope Francis raised her day, July 22, from a memorial to a feast, the same rank as the feasts of the apostles, and the decree used that old title.
screen: `WOMAN, WHY WEEPEST THOU?` · `ONE WORD: MARY.` · `DON'T CLING; GO AND TELL.` · `JULY 22, A FEAST SINCE 2016.` · then, large: `APOSTLE TO THE APOSTLES.`

segments.voice: Think back over the last week or so for something genuinely good: a recovery, a kindness you saw, a small win, a reconciliation, a baby, a sunrise, and let it fill your chest for a moment. Then think of who would be glad to hear it, and picture their face. If you pray, hold Mary's words, I have seen the Lord, and give thanks; if you don't, just enjoy the good news.
Apostle. One who is sent: the title given to Mary Magdalene after Jesus sent her to tell the disciples he was risen. Today's word.
Your line: I have seen the lord. The first one sent was the one who stayed. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 531 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: RECEIVE YE THE HOLY GHOST.`

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate the Feast of Saint Mary Magdalene on July 22, with the Gloria at Mass and her encounter with the risen Jesus read as the Gospel.

chat.says: Why is Mary Magdalene called the apostle to the apostles?
options: Jesus sent her to tell the disciples he was risen, and apostle means one who is sent.
Because she later became the leader of the twelve apostles in Jerusalem.
Because Pope Francis gave her that brand-new title in 2016, the first time.
chat.meaning: Jesus sent her: go to my brethren. She told them, I have seen the Lord. Apostle means one who is sent.

Rabboni.meaning: Master: Mary's word when she knew him

Mary Magdalene.meaning: the woman sent to tell the disciples he was risen

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): hook no longer tells the listener what 'anyone who has lost someone knows'; 'hundreds of paintings', 'the first person in John's Gospel sent' and 'very early' softened (word, teach, trapdoor); trapdoor's uncited Rabanus Maurus/Aquinas line replaced with the cited 2016 decree.
'Woman, why weepest thou?' and her answer are given without quotation marks; close to Douay wording.
Feast of St. Mary Magdalene: decree dated June 3, 2016, at Pope Francis's wish; the decree and an accompanying article by Archbishop Roche used 'apostolorum apostola'. Confirm.
'Very early, Christian writers gave her a title': often traced to Hippolytus (who calls the women 'apostles to the apostles') and later to Rabanus Maurus and Aquinas. Confirm wording.
Mē mou haptou as 'don't cling / hold on to me': widely accepted reading of the present imperative. Confirm.
